                                  EXCEPTIONS TO THE PFD ​
                             OF INTERVENOR GRETCHEN NOELKE

COMES NOW, Gretchen Noelke, pro se and through her Agent George Noelke, to submit her Exceptions
to the PFD in this case.

I.​    Introduction
      A.​ Intervenor Gretchen Noelke’s last filed documents in this case was her Post Hearing Reply Brief.
          See Item 6386. ​


      B.​ The PFD does not approve any route going through her ranch, (She specifically opposes Routes
          487, 494 and 499, all of which include Link M7; she also opposes Routes 547, 548, 295, 296
          and 297, all of which include Link M22.) Instead, the PFD recommends denial of the CCNs in
          59475 and 59182. In the alternative, if the Commission must select a route then it recommends
          Applicants “best meets” route, 894. Route 894 does not traverse her ranch.​


      C.​ Also, as set forth in her Reply Brief, she “aligns herself with American Stewards of Liberty and
          the other Intervenors arguing that Applicants have failed to establish a need for this project.” See
          Reply Brief, page 2, Item 6386. She does not, however, agree with American Stewards of Liberty
        on the issue of abating the 765 kV cases until the next legislative session.​


   D.​ Applicants did not directly or indirectly rebut any fact she had admitted into evidence.

11. Changes to the PFD

   A.​ Gretchen Noelke agrees with the conclusion of the PFD that the CCN’s in both 59475 and 59182
       should be denied. She recommends no additional Findings of Fact or Conclusions of Law for the
       PFD.​


   B.​ She specifically supports Conclusion of Law Number 13, which finds ERCOT’s Permian Basin
       Reliability Project recommendation is not entitled to great weight in the determination of need for
       this reliability project. PFD page 195. This is consistent with her earlier position, as set forth in
       I.d. above.​


   C.​ She objects to the alternate conclusion of the PFD that, if the Commission must select a route,
       then Route 894 should be selected. Throughout this case, she has avoided taking the position that
       another route is preferable to a route that impacts her ranch. As such, she recommends deletion
       of Conclusion of Law Number 16 and its supporting facts, which in the alternative of denial
       recommends Route 894.The denial of the CCN’s in the present version of the PFD is sound, and
       an alternative conclusion recommending a specific route is not legally necessary.

WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Intervenor Gretchen Noelke respectfully prays for the
deletion of Conclusion of Law Number 16, and its supporting fact, recommending Route 894. Otherwise,
the Findings of Fact and Conclusion that support the denial of CCN 59475 and 59182 must be
AFFIRMED.

Signed September 2, 2026

Respectfully submitted,

​
/s/Gretchen Noelke by Agent George Noelke​
Gretchen Noelke by Agent George Noelke​
Intervenor​
Pro se Landowner
